newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE AIMS TO IMPROVE COMPETITIVENESS, EMPLOYMENT.
newsitem.headline: GREECE AIMS TO IMPROVE COMPETITIVENESS, EMPLOYMENT.

text.p: Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis told a news conference on Thursday that increasing economic competitiveness and employment were among Greece's priorities in 1997.

"Investments must be made in order to increase employment and improve living conditions. The Develpment Ministry will be behind such actions," Simitis told the news conference also headed by Development Minister Vasso Papandreou.
Simitis said the use of natural gas in industrial units would be cost effective, environment friendly and bear economic benefits that will be spread in the next few years.
Greece should prepare for the liberalization of electrical power in 2001 and create renewable sources of energy, he said.
With regard to industrial policy, emphasis will be given to medium-sized enterprises and enhance product quality.
The state has earmarked 34 billion drachmas for laboratory facilities that will set product standards, Simitis added.
But absorption of European Union funds for the industrial sector was not satisfactory although it had risen from 12 percent in 1995 to 30 percent in 1996, said the premier.
Development Minister Vasso Papandreou also touched upon quality and energy issues.
"We have thought of calling 1998 a year for quality," Papandreou said. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
